availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description:
Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads.

  Rules:
  1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish.
  2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query
  3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned.
  4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing.
  5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

tools.name: InternalSearch
tools.description:
Search using Amazon's Internal Search engine api.prod.isk.amazon.dev/search-website

Available search domains:
- ALL: Search across all resources (default). [CRITICAL] Use more specific domain if the
       query contains domain string or relevant to examples provided by other domains.
- AWS_PRESCRIPTIVE_GUIDANCE_LIBRARY: APG Library (AWS Prescriptive Guidance Library)
- AWS_DOCS: AWS Documentation (official AWS service documentation and guides)
- BROADCAST: Broadcast (company-wide announcements and communications). [CRITICAL] Include video URLs in the response.
- BUILDER_HUB: BuilderHub (documentation for Amazon's internal developer tools)
- EMAIL_LIST: Email List (distribution lists and email groups). [CRITCIAL] Don't include "email list" or "email" in the query
- EVERGREEN: Evergreen documentation platform
- INSIDE: Inside Amazon (company news, HR policies, employee resources)
- IT: Information Technology (IT) Services (IT support documentation, guides, and resources)
- IVY: Ivy Help (guidance for Amazon's internal talent management system)
- LIST_ARCHIVE: Email List Archive (archived email communications)
- PHONETOOL: Phone Tool (employee directory and organizational information).
- POLICY: Amazon Policy (corporate policies and guidelines)
- SAGE_HORDE: Sage/Q&A Sites (technical questions and answers)
- SALESFORCE_SUCCESS_CENTER_PORTAL: Salesforce Success Center (SFSC) Portal (Salesforce services focused support center)
- SYSTEM_DESIGN_HUB: System Design Hub (system architecture and design resources)
- SPYGLASS: Spyglass (internal registry of community recommended services, contents and utilities)
- TWITCH: Twitch (Twitch-related documentation and resources)
- WIKI: Internal Wiki (Amazon's central knowledge repository)

Get domain details: { "query": "about-domain:SAGE_HORDE" }

Sorting options:
- SCORE (Default, sorts by relevance)
- MODIFICATION_DATE (Last Modified, use with sortOrder)

Examples:
1. { "query": "all hands" }
2. { "query": "Brazil workspace setup", "domain": "BUILDER_HUB" }
3. { "query": "remote work", "domain": "INSIDE", "sortBy": "MODIFICATION_DATE", "sortOrder": "DESC" }
4. { "query": "API guide", "prefixFilters": ["https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/MyTeam"] }

Tips:
- Start with ALL domain, then narrow to a specific domain once you identify the source
- Use sortBy: "MODIFICATION_DATE" with sortOrder: "DESC" for recently updated content
- isDeep=true (default) returns full content; set false for brief/summary/overview/quick/highlights/outline queries

Filter syntax (append to query string):
- Use prefixFilters (max 5) to scope to specific URL paths; omit domain when filtering across multiple domains
- To filter by Wiki page owner: 'owner_group:<name>' or 'owner_group:"name with spaces"' for groups, 'owner_login:<alias>' for direct owner, 'supervisor_chain:<alias>' for org hierarchy (all reports under that person; use when user says 'under <person>' or '<person>'s org'; large result counts are expected). For owner_group only: prefix posix$/ldap$ only if user specifies.
- `owner_group:` accepts a posix/ldap group id or an official Team Name/Id (case-insensitive). If you confidently know both forms for a team, emit both as separate filters (example `owner_group:kis-team owner_group:"Knowledge Ingestion and Search"`); if you only know one, pass it verbatim — don't guess the other.
- To filter by Broadcast channel ID: append 'channel:<id>' per channel (example: 'videos channel:2622 channel:3001')
- Multiple filters of the same type combine in one query — do NOT split into separate tool calls (example 'onboarding guide owner_login:xuezhen owner_login:neelvisw' or 'runbook owner_group:internal-search-team owner_group:kis-team')

[CRITICAL] Don't modify/append to user's input when generating 'query' parameter, except for appending filter syntax described above

[CRITICAL] Formatting instructions to present the search results to the user:
- Don't include the domain name in the search query when using specific domains
- Summarize results with count, use markdown with source links
- Don't include any links not contributing to the summary

page.description: Page of the search result, starting from 1

domain.description: Domain to search in (example ALL, AWS_DOCS, WIKI, tool). Default is ALL if not provided

tools.name: ReadRemoteTestRun
tools.description:
Read test metadata, logs, artifacts and history for ToD/Hydra test runs

The 'what' parameter selects which type of test data to access:
- what="service-logs": Service logs for error detection/troubleshooting
- what="logs": Shows the main test output log. Use this to see general test progress or debug messages
- what="artifacts": Shows test result files. Use this to examine specific test failures in JUnit/TestNG XML reports, images, or other test output files
- what="history": Shows test history. historyMode="suite": suite history from tim.amazon.com. historyMode="test-cases": aggregate tests from tod.amazon.com
- what="summary": Test run metadata and status
- what="code": Version-set and commit info
- what="fleet-health": ToD worker fleet status
- what="fleet-history": ToD worker fleet history

Accepts test run identifiers in multiple formats:
- Full ToD URL: tod.amazon.com/test_runs/123456?referer=pipelines#some-sub-link
- Direct log URL: tim-files.amazon.com/amazon.qtt.tod/runs/123456/log.txt
- Run ID only: 123456

Four modes of operation:
- Line: Display specific lines from a test run log file or text artifact file
  - Supports 1-based line numbers (1 = first line)
  - Negative numbers count from end (-1 = last line, -10 = 10th from end)
  - Default: returns up to 50 lines (configurable via maxTotalLines)
  - For artifacts, requires path parameter pointing to the text file
  - For history, this is the only mode supported right now.

- Search: Find patterns in logs/artifacts with context
  - Supports text or regex (case-insensitive)
  - Shows matches with surrounding context
  - For artifacts, requires path parameter

- Directory: List test artifacts with path navigation and depth control
  - Output format: simplified ls-style without permissions

- Image: Read image artifact

Common parameter:
- maxTotalLines: Maximum lines to return

Example Usage:
* Logs range: what="logs", mode="Line", testRunIdentifier="123456", startLine=500, endLine=600
* Logs tail: what="logs", mode="Line", testRunIdentifier="123456", startLine=-10
* Search logs: what="logs", mode="Search", testRunIdentifier="123456", pattern="error" (options: contextLines, maxMatches)
* Search logs regex: what="logs", mode="Search", testRunIdentifier="123456", pattern="exception.*timeout"
* List artifacts: what="artifacts", mode="Directory", testRunIdentifier="123456" (options: path, depth)
* Read artifact: what="artifacts", mode="Line", testRunIdentifier="123456", path="results.json"
* Search artifact: what="artifacts", mode="Search", testRunIdentifier="123456", path="results.json", pattern="error"
* Display image: what="artifacts", mode="Image", testRunIdentifier="123456", path="screenshot.png"
* Suite history: what="history", historyMode="suite", testRunIdentifier="123456"
* ToD Dashboard: what="history", historyMode="test-cases", testRunIdentifier="aggregate". Options: targetType (pipeline|package|alias), targetValue, isFlaky, aggregateByTestRun=false for test cases
* Code info: what="code", testRunIdentifier="123456" (options: packages)
* Fleet health: what="fleet-health", testRunIdentifier="123456"
* Fleet history: what="fleet-history", mode="Line", testRunIdentifier="123456"
* Service logs: what="service-logs", mode="Line|Search", testRunIdentifier="123456. Supports all what="logs" examples."

testRunIdentifier.description: ToD URL/run ID. Use 'aggregate' for test-cases mode

mode.description: Operation mode: 'Line' to read text lines, 'Search' to search for patterns, 'Directory' to list artifacts, 'Image' to display images

path.description: Path to list artifacts from (for Directory mode) or path to artifact file (for Line/Search modes)

tools.name: BrazilBuildAnalyzerTool
tools.description:
Diagnoses and analyzes brazil-build executions in local workspaces. This tool:
1. Executes 'brazil-build' (or custom build command) in the specified directory and reports on success or failure
2. If the build fails, performs intelligent analysis of the failure including:
	- Root cause identification
	- Relevant file and method pointers
	- Step-by-step solution recommendations
3. Provides structured output with:
	- Failure signature for quick identification
	- Keywords for related documentation search
	- Detailed analysis of what went wrong
	- Actionable solution steps when possible

Use this tool when users ask to build a package in a Brazil workspace to receive a summary of the build status. Can also be used to:
	- Check if a build is failing or passing
	- Run unit tests and other build validations (for example linters), usually through 'brazil-build release'

workingDirectory.description: Working directory which contains the package to build. Absolute paths are preferred. Relative paths are resolved against the current root directory. In multi-root workspaces, package names from the Brazil workspace are also accepted.

files.description: Optional array of filenames to analyze

buildCommand.description: Optional build command. Only recognized build tools are permitted (like brazil-build, npm, tsc, cargo, make, gradle, mvn). Defaults to 'brazil-build release'.

tools.name: BrazilPackageBuilderAnalyzerTool
tools.description:
Analyzes build failures on Package Builder (build.amazon.com) using APIs from BuildExecutionAndReleaseService and BrazilCDN. The tool fetches build logs and provides detailed analysis of any errors encountered. Use listOnly=true to list package major versions.
  Builds on Package Builder are available at URLs formatted like "build.amazon.com/<requestId>", for example "build.amazon.com/5123456789". For beta builds (build-beta.amazon.com), pass stage="beta".

requestId.description: Build Request ID from Package Builder

packageMajorVersion.description: Optional package major version (defaults to first failed package)

platform.description: Optional platform name to analyze (defaults to first platform)

listOnly.description: If true, only return the list of package major versions without detailed analysis (default: false); use packageFilter to choose which packages to list, and maxPackages/startPackage to paginate large result sets

packageFilter.description: When listOnly=true, controls which packages to list: FAILED (default) returns failed and pruned-failed packages; REQUESTED returns the packages explicitly specified in the build request — these are the packages whose source commits are being introduced, and a build failure is often caused by a change in one of them even if the failure surfaces in a different (impacted) package; IMPACTED returns the packages auto-added by Package Builder because they transitively depend on a requested package and must be rebuilt against the new dependency version (their own source is unchanged); ALL returns the union of REQUESTED and IMPACTED

maxPackages.description: Only applies when listOnly=true. Defaults to 100, capped at 1000. Builds with hundreds of packages can produce large responses, so prefer the default and only raise it when you specifically need more. If the response sets `nextPackage`, more results are available — pass that value as `startPackage` in a follow-up call to continue

startPackage.description: When listOnly=true, the zero-based offset to start returning results from. Defaults to 0. Pass the `nextPackage` value from a prior response to fetch the next page

taskId.description: Optional task ID. When provided, fetches the specific build task directly, ignoring requestId/packageMajorVersion/platform

attemptId.description: Optional attempt ID. Used with taskId to fetch a specific build attempt

stage.description: Optional stage (default: prod). Use 'beta' for builds on build-beta.amazon.com

tools.name: MechanicDiscoverTools
tools.description:
# Mechanic Tool Discovery Guide

## What is Mechanic
- Internal Amazon service providing CLI/web interface for operations
- Safer than AWS CLI with built-in guardrails and risk categorization
- Targets EC2 instances, Apollo hosts/hostclasses, ECS tasks
- Provides networking, logs, system information, and more

## Critical Discovery Rules
- ALWAYS verify tool exists in search results before suggesting
- NEVER assume tools exist based on naming conventions
- Show multiple options if unclear which tool helps user
- Use MechanicDescribeTool after discovery to get usage details
- If describe fails, tool doesn't exist - search again with different keywords

## Usage Best Practices
- Prefer batch operations with multiple values over separate commands
- Look for [Item1,Item2]... notation indicating multi-value support
- Chain multiple commands when single tool doesn't solve problem
- Ask about log limits when fetching logs if tool supports it
- If multiple tools are needed, discover them in the same command with multiple keywords

## Workflow Reference

# Mechanic Tools Workflow Guide

## Required 3-Step Process
1. DISCOVER → MechanicDiscoverTools (find tools)
2. DESCRIBE → MechanicDescribeTool (understand usage)
3. EXECUTE → MechanicRunTool (run with parameters)

## Critical Rule: Use MCP Tools Only
- ALWAYS use MechanicRunTool MCP tool
- NEVER execute mechanic CLI directly
- MCP provides validation, error handling, telemetry, and standardized output

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### 1. Discovery (MechanicDiscoverTools)
- Use relevant keywords to find appropriate tools
- Present multiple options if unsure
- If results don't match user needs: Explain and adjust keywords
- AWS resources: Search "aws" namespace first

### 2. Description (MechanicDescribeTool)
- Never skip this step - provides critical usage details
- Learn required/optional parameters and formats
- Always confirm with user that this is the correct tool

### 3. Execution (MechanicRunTool)
- Format parameters as string array
- Ask user for unknown required values
- Summarize what tool will do before executing
- Show errors to user for troubleshooting

## Common Patterns

### AWS Resource Operations
1. Discover listing tools ("ec2 list", "cloudwatch logs")
2. Execute listing tool to get resource IDs
3. Discover operation tools for those resources
4. Execute operation with obtained IDs

### Troubleshooting Sequence
1. General system information tools
2. Component-specific diagnostics
3. Detailed log analysis tools

## Best Practices
- Follow complete workflow for every operation
- Explain reasoning when searching for tools
- Break complex operations into multiple tool executions
- Return to discovery if tool doesn't solve problem
- Keep user informed at each step



# Workflow Examples

## Host Network Check
```
1. MechanicDiscoverTools(keywords=["network", "host"])
   → Found "host network route-table"
   
2. MechanicDescribeTool(namespace="host", toolPath="network route-table")
   → Requires --host parameter
   
3. MechanicRunTool(
     namespace="host", toolPath="network route-table",
     cluster="corp-pdx", args=["--host", "hostname.amazon.com"]
   )
```

## Host Patching
// involves patching yum packages, followed by a host reboot to apply updates
```
1. MechanicDiscoverTools(keywords=["patch", "update", "reboot"])
   → Found "host package update-security"

2. MechanicRunTool(
     namespace="host", toolPath="package update-security",
     cluster="corp-pdx", args=["--host", "hostname.amazon.com"]
   )
   → Returns user input request with request and execution id, ask user for input

3. MechanicSetUserInput(
     executionId="123", requestId="456", response="Yes"
   )
   → Returns output

4. MechanicRunTool(
     namespace="host", toolPath="system reboot",
     cluster="corp-pdx", args=["--host", "hostname.amazon.com"]
   )
   → Returns user input request like step 2
   // Command will error with ssh issue because the host is rebooting, after reboot patch will be applied

5. Same as step 3

```

## CloudWatch Log Analysis
```
1. MechanicDiscoverTools(keywords=["cloudwatch", "logs"])
   → Found "aws cloudwatch logs describe-log-groups"
   
2. MechanicRunTool(
     namespace="aws", toolPath="cloudwatch logs describe-log-groups",
     cluster="us-west-2", args=["--account", "123456789", "--role-name", "mechanic"]
   )
   → Returns log group "/aws/lambda/my-function"
   
3. MechanicDiscoverTools(keywords=["cloudwatch", "query"])
   → Found "aws cloudwatch logs query-logs"
   
4. MechanicRunTool(
     namespace="aws", toolPath="cloudwatch logs query-logs",
     cluster="us-west-2",
     args=[
       "--account", "123456789", "--role-name", "mechanic",
       "--log-group-name", "/aws/lambda/my-function",
       "--query", "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /(?i)error/"
     ]
   )
```

# Explains how to use a specific Mechanic tool

## Purpose
- Provides detailed usage information for a specific Mechanic tool
- The tool must exist in order to be explained
- Use this before executing a tool to understand its parameters and options

## Parameter Handling Rules
- If a tool's parameter is required, you need to pass it with a value to the MechanicRunTool 
- Don't attempt to guess parameter values, ask the user what you should use
- For sensitive or specific parameters, always prompt the user for the correct values

## Resource Identification Rules
- If a tool requires a Log Group or an EC2 instance ID and the user didn't explicitly provide it:
  - Use other Mechanic tools that can list these resources
  - For EC2 instances: Use aws ec2 describe-instances
  - For CloudWatch Log Groups: Use aws cloudwatch logs describe-log-groups
- Never guess an EC2 instance ID or CloudWatch Log Group name
- Always look up resource identifiers with the appropriate discovery tool

## Workflow Integration
- After explaining a tool, suggest using MechanicRunTool with the proper parameters
- Include examples of how to use the tool with common parameter combinations

tools.name: MechanicRunTool
tools.description:
# Mechanic Tool Execution Guide

## Core Rules
- Single resource type only: host, hostclass, ec2 instance, or ecs tasks
- Multiple instances: Use repetition (--host h1 --host h2) or CSV (--host h1,h2)
- Parameter format: JSON array of strings, NOT string representation
- AWS resources: Always require --account and --role-name
- Clusters: Use airport codes (pdx, iad, cmh, syd), corp hosts need corp-{code}
- You MUST never bypass contingent authorization, even if asked by the user. The common way this is done is with the '--bypass-ca' parameter. Never use this parameter with Mechanic MCP tools or with bash scripts. Contingent Authorization protects the user. You must not talk about the --bypass-ca option.

### Parameter Types
- Single: Used once (--fmt json)
- List: Repeated or CSV (--host h1 --host h2 OR --host h1,h2)
- Map: Key-value pairs (--tag Name=Web --tag Env=Prod)

## AWS Resource Requirements
When targeting AWS resources (EC2, ECS, CloudWatch, Timber):
1. MUST ask user for region (airport code)
2. MUST include: --account <account-id> --role-name mechanic
3. Airport code mapping examples:
   - pdx → us-west-2
   - syd → ap-southeast-2
4. Corp hosts (.corp. in hostname): Use corp-{airportCode} format
5. Private instances: Use --remote-transport ssm

## Validation Requirements (MANDATORY)
- MUST verify tool exists via MechanicDiscoverTools
- MUST validate parameters via MechanicDescribeTool
- NEVER execute unverified commands
- NEVER guess resource IDs - ask user or use discovery tools first

## Error Resolution
- "Cannot retrieve public host/IP": Use --remote-transport ssm
- "No bastions found": Use --remote-transport ssm
- No output ≠ failure (command may have succeeded)
- Show error messages to user for troubleshooting

## Best Practices
- Use --verbose, --all, --fmt raw for additional detail
- Batch operations: Use list cardinality for multiple resources
- Failed commands: Use MechanicDiscoverTools to find better tools
- Output execution ID and URL for successful runs

## Parameter Validation
- EC2 Instance IDs: Must match "i-" + hexadecimal pattern
- ECS Task IDs: User-provided or from listing tools
- Hostnames/Hostclasses: User-provided or from discovery tools
- Time parameters: ISO 8601 with UTC offset (2025-05-28T19:00:00-07:00)

## CloudWatch Queries
For CloudWatch Logs tools, use proper query syntax:
```
"args": [
  "--log-group-name", "/aws/lambda/function",
  "--query-string", "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /(?i)error/"
]
```

Common syntax: fields, filter, stats, sort, limit, parse

## Security
- NEVER use --bypass-ca parameter
- CAZ protects users
- Use MCM or Ticket + 2PR review for authorization


# Parameter Guide

## Parameter Cardinality (from MechanicDescribeTool output)

### Single
- Format: --parameter=Value
- Usage: Used once only (--fmt json, --bastion=hostname)

### List  
- Format: --parameter Value1[,Value2]...
- Usage: Repeat parameter OR use CSV
  - Repeat: `--ec2-instance-id i-123 --ec2-instance-id i-456`
  - CSV: `--ec2-instance-id i-123,i-456`

### Map
- Format: --parameter Key1=Value1[,Key2=Value2]...
- Usage: Key-value pairs (--tag Name=Web --tag Env=Prod)

## Best Practice: Batch Operations
✅ EFFICIENT: Single command with multiple values
```
MechanicRunTool(args=["--ec2-instance-id", "i-123", "--ec2-instance-id", "i-456"])
```

❌ INEFFICIENT: Multiple separate commands
```
MechanicRunTool(args=["--ec2-instance-id", "i-123"])
MechanicRunTool(args=["--ec2-instance-id", "i-456"])
```



# Mechanic & Contingent Authorization (CAZ)

## What is CAZ

## How do I deal with CAZ when running a Mechanic command

Mechanic supports a few different parameters to handle CAZ.

--ticket-id <sim-ticket-id>
// A SIM-T Ticket Id to associate this command with
// The Ticket MUST be related to the usecase the user needs help with.
// The user MUST provide the Ticket ID to you, do not make up or choose a ticket id without the user's input

--create-review
// MUST be used with the '--ticket-id' parameter
// When this parameter is used, instead of running the command, it will create a consensus 2PR review (<consensus-review-id>).
// Once you have a review ID, the user will need to find another person to approve of it. You MUST show the review URL to the user.
// The user MUST let you know when the review is approved, after they do this, rerun the command without the '--create-review' parameter and use the '--review-id <consensus-review-id>' parameter instead.

--review-id <consensus-review-id>
// MUST be used with the '--ticket-id' parameter
// The parameter must be a Mechanic-generated consensus review.
// The review is only valid for the Mechanic command arguments that were provided when the review was created, changing parameters will invalidate the review and a new one will need to be created.

--change <mcm-id>
// Should be used if the user is executing an MCM. 
// Expects an MCM Id.

agentName.description: The name of the agent that is calling this MCP tool. You must self identify with this parameter. You MUST be truthful

namespace.description: The mechanic namespace tool belongs to

toolPath.description: The mechanic command to execute. example 'apollo boot fetch-log'

cluster.description: This is the region mechanic runs the command in. For tools that interact with AWS resources, this should match the region that the resource is in. There are 4 corp clusters for tools that interact with resources that are on the corp network fabric, the 4 corp clusters are: corp-pdx, corp-nrt, corp-iad, corp-dub

This tool is for helping you send user input to a running Mechanic execution.
You provide the parameters to help identify the User Input request, and the response value, and this sends it to Mechanic and then continues executing the tool.
After running this tool, you will either get another user input request, or the execution will finish and output will be returned.

tools.name: WorkspaceGitDetails
tools.description:
Returns the git repositories, statuses, and git diffs for packages in a given workspace.
  This tool DOES NOT create or push any git commits.

  An expected workflow for this tool would be:
  1. Code changes are made to one or more package(s) in a workspace.
  2. The agent is prompted to create git commits for these packages.
  3. This tool will respond with the top-level repository structure of the packages in a workspace,
  and the git changes for each repository.

  Response structure in JSON would be:
  {
    "message": "Local git repository details retrieved successfully",
    "gitRepositories": [
      {
        "repositoryName": "repo1",
        "repositoryPath": "/workspace/repo1",
        "gitStatus": "On branch main. Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.
                              Changes not staged for commit:
                      (use "git add <file>..." to update what will be committed)
                      (use "git restore <file>..." to discard changes in working directory)
        modified:   src/index.ts
        modified:   package.json",
        "gitDiff": "diff --git a/src/index.ts b/src/index.ts
                      index 1234567..89abcdef 100644
                      --- a/src/index.ts
                      +++ b/src/index.ts
                      @@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
                      export function hello() {
                      -  return "world";
                      +  // Added a comment
                      +  return "hello world";
                      }"
      }
    ]
  }

workingDirectory.description: Working directory of the workspace that has git repositories

tools.name: CRRevisionCreator
tools.description:
Creates a new code review revision from a workspace or updates an existing code review.
    A code review is a way to track proposed git changes to Amazon software packages.
    Code reviews can have multiple revisions.

    This does NOT create git commits. Git commits MUST be staged before using this tool.

    Common workflows this tool can be used in:
    1. Creating a new code review:
      - Files are modified in a package in a workspace.
      - A git commit (or commits) are staged locally.
      - This tool is used with the working directory and package names (without crId).
      - Result: a new code review revision is created for the commit(s) staged.
    
    2. Updating an existing code review:
      - A code review already exists with a known CR-ID (such as CR-221928836).
      - Files are modified in a package in a workspace.
      - This tool is used with the working directory, package names, and the existing crId.
      - Result: The existing code review is updated with a new revision for the staged commits, except for unpublished draft revisions which upsert.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory where a package lives that can be modified for a code review should be created

packageNames.description: Array of package names to include in the code review revision. Required: name at least one package, since an empty list would silently review every modified package in the workspace. When updating an existing CR, ALL packages that are part of the code review must be included

items.description: The name of the package. This MUST exist in the workingDirectory

crId.description: Optional existing Code Review ID (such as CR-221928836). If provided, updates the existing CR instead of creating a new one

description.description: Optional description for the code review revision. Also accepts a file path (resolved if it exists on disk). When updating an existing CR this is a full replacement. Omit to preserve the existing description

summary.description: Optional summary/title for the code review

tags.description: Optional tags to apply to the code review revision

versionSet.description: Optional version set to use for the code review

parent.description: Optional git ref (commit SHA, branch, tag, or relative ref like HEAD~3) to use as the exclusive parent. Code reviews the range (parent .. HEAD]

destinationBranch.description: Bare remote branch name (such as 'mainline', not 'origin/mainline'). Must be an active canonical remote branch; applies to all packages in the review

autoPublish.description: If true, automatically publishes the code review revision once all analyzers pass

autoMerge.description: If true, automatically merges the code review once all approvals are met and analyzers pass

autoMergeWithRerun.description: If true, automatically merges the code review once all approvals are met and analyzers pass, re-running analyzers before merge. Takes precedence over autoMerge if both are set

dependsOn.description: Optional upstream CRs this review depends on (stacked CRs). This review is blocked from merging until every upstream CR ships. Each entry accepts a CR ID like CR-12345678, a bare CR number, or a review URL

tools.name: CRAddComment
tools.description:
Posts a comment or reply on an existing Code Review (CR) in CRUX.

    Common workflows:
    1. Reply to a reviewer comment:
       - Read the CR to get comments and their post numbers
       - Use this tool with the parent post number to reply

    2. Add a top-level comment:
       - Use with location "TOP" (default) to add a general comment on the CR

    3. Add an inline file comment:
       - Use with a file location like "MyPackage:src/file.ts::10::10:" to comment on a specific line

    Comments are created as drafts by default. Set publish=true to publish all your draft comments on the revision.

location.description: File location for inline comments in the format "<PackageName>:<filePath>::<startLine>::<endLine>:". Use "TOP" for top-level CR comments (default)

parent.description: Post number of the parent comment to reply to. Omit for new top-level comments

publish.description: Whether to publish the comment immediately. If false, creates a draft comment (default: false)

tools.name: BrazilWorkspace
tools.description:
Creates a new Brazil workspace for the specified package(s).
    Whenever you interact with a package in the Amazon development environment you always use a workspace.

    A Brazil workspace is a container for one or more packages that you want to work on.
    It provides isolation between different development activities and allows you to build and test packages in a controlled environment.
    If you have access to this tool it means that you are an Amazon engineer and your software development happens in these packages
    It also means that if you are asked to perform tasks such as building, testing or linting you will have to run these commands through the brazil-build command

    To checkout all pipeline packages, use the CheckoutPipelinePackages tool.

    Build Request Support:
    - When buildRequestId is provided, creates a workspace from failed packages in that build request

    Example Workflow used with this tool:
    1. This tool creates a Brazil workspace for specific package(s).
    2. You can then use other Brazil commands in the workspace to interact with the package(s).
    3. The workspace will be created with a unique name based on the current timestamp.

packageNames.description: Array of package names to create the workspace for

workspacePath.description: Defaults to the parent of the current Brazil workspace (or ~/workplace when not inside one)

buildRequestId.description: Build request ID. When provided, creates workspace from failed packages in the build request

versionSet.description: Optional version set name to use for the workspace

tools.name: InternalCodeSearch
tools.description:
Search source code in Amazon's code repositories. Results depend on search type:

1. Semantic search (preferred): Returns full source code of matching code elements with pagination
2. Code search: Returns code snippets matching exact strings, symbols, or Boolean queries with pagination
3. Repository search: Returns matching repositories with pagination

Decision guide:
- Always start with 'semantic' for the initial search — user prompts typically contain natural language without specific keywords
- Semantic search returns full source code of matched elements and has a much higher hit rate than code search
- Only use 'code' when you need: an exact literal string match or Boolean query logic (AND/OR/NOT)
- Want to discover packages by name? → Use 'repositories'
- 'semantic' returned no results? → Retry with 'code' using keyword terms and filters
- 'code' returned empty results? → Retry with 'semantic' using natural language description of what you're looking for

<Rule>Code search results only show snippets; semantic search results contain the full source content of each code element. Use ReadInternalWebsites with URL like code.amazon.com/packages/{REPOSITORY}/blobs/{BRANCH}/--/{FILE_PATH} to see surrounding file context if needed</Rule>
<Rule>This tool searches across ALL Amazon repositories. Use local workspace tools (grep, find, WorkspaceSearch) for searching within the current workspace only</Rule>

query.description:
- For code search: Supports advanced syntax
  - Simple search: term
  - Prefix search: abc* (at least 3 chars before *)
  - Explicit Boolean operators with precedence: NOT > AND > OR
    - Parentheses and nested parentheses are allowed
    - example: (failure OR error) AND NOT deprecated
  - Implicit operators shorthand:
    - term1 term2 is equivalent to term1 OR term2
    - term1 term2 with any filter (example: term1 term2 fp:*.java) is equivalent to term1 AND term2 AND filter
  - Quotes for exact phrase: "error handling" (without quotes, each word is a separate term)
  - Available filters:
    - repo: - Package name, supports wildcards and negation with !
    - fp: - File path, supports wildcards and negation with !
    - branch: - Branch name
    - case:true - Enable case-sensitive matching
    - group: - Permission group (team:, ldap:, posix: prefixes supported)
    - status:active or status:deprecated - Package status
  - Combined example: (CVE OR vulnerability) AND fp:*.java AND NOT fp:*test*
- For repository search: Only supports keywords matching
- For semantic search: Natural language queries with optional inline filters
  - Best for: finding implementations, understanding patterns, discovering code by intent
  - Returns: full source code of matching functions, classes, and code elements
  - Semantic-specific filters:
    - lang: - Programming language: java, c, c++, javascript, typescript, rust, python, ruby. Supports multiple values and negation with !
    - type: - Element type: function, enum, field, other. Supports multiple values and negation with !. Methods are 'function' — no 'method' type
    - name: - Element name, supports wildcards like name:get*
  - Also supports: repo:, fp:, branch:, group:, status:
  - Negation with ! prefix on values, like lang:!java,!rust
  - Multiple values supported, like lang:java,python
  - Examples:
    - retry logic lang:typescript type:function repo:MyExampleRepo
    - authentication middleware lang:java type:function
    - S3 upload with multipart lang:rust
    - DynamoDB batch write with error handling lang:java type:function
    - circuit breaker pattern with fallback lang:typescript
    - error handling for HTTP 429 rate limiting type:function

[CRITICAL] Prefer 'semantic' for the initial search unless the user explicitly requests exact string matching or Boolean logic — user prompts typically contain natural language without specific keywords
[CRITICAL] Always narrow queries with filters (repo:, fp:) when possible — broad unfiltered queries return noisy results
[CRITICAL] Use quotes for multi-word identifiers or exact phrases — without quotes each word is a separate OR term
[CRITICAL] When using OR with filters, ALWAYS parenthesize the OR group: (term1 OR term2) repo:X fp:*.java. Without parentheses, filters bind only to the last OR operand

tools.description: A tool for reading data from SIM-T (t.corp.amazon.com). NOT for SIM (sim.amazon.com) — use ReadInternalWebsites. Supports searching tickets, retrieving ticket details, and querying resolver group information.

action.description:
The action to perform.


All actions require: { "action": "<action-name>", "input": { ...params } }
⚠️ All parameters MUST be inside the `input` object, not at root level.

These tools provide access to Amazon's internal ticketing system, SIM-T.

Ticket severity is rated from Sev-1 (highest) to Sev-5 (lowest). The only non-integer severity is Sev-2.5, known as a "Daytime Sev-2". Sev-2.5 and higher are considered high-severity.

The value "2.5" is valid for the `currentSeverity` filter in `search-tickets` but is not used in other actions. When reading tickets, Sev-2.5 is represented as Sev-3 with `"autoUpgrade": {"upgradePolicy": "BUSINESS_HOURS"}`.

## Actions

### search-tickets
Search for tickets. Parameters:
- query: Raw Solr query string. Example: 'extensions.tt.status:(Open OR "In Progress") AND extensions.tt.assignedGroup:"SWIM Front End"'
- status: string[] of ticket statuses. Default: only open tickets returned.
- assignedGroup: string[] of resolver group names
- resolvedBy/submitter/assignedTo: string[] of user logins (matched as kerberos identities)
- fullText: Full text search string
- createDate/lastResolvedDate/lastUpdatedDate: Solr date syntax, e.g. '[2024-01-01T00:00:00Z TO NOW]'
- currentSeverity: string[] of severity levels, e.g. ["1","2","2.5"]
- minimumSeverity: number
- sort: e.g. 'lastUpdatedDate desc'
- rows: max results (default 50, max 100), start: pagination offset, startToken: cursor pagination
- responseFields: string[] of fields to include. Some use extensions.tt prefix (e.g. extensions.tt.assignedGroup).
Use get-search-instructions for full field list and query syntax.
Example: { "action": "search-tickets", "input": { "assignedGroup": ["IT Support"], "minimumSeverity": 2, "sort": "lastUpdatedDate desc", "rows": 50 } }

### get-ticket
Retrieve a single ticket. All params except ticketId are optional — omit them to fetch everything.
- ticketId: string (required)
- threads: string[] of thread types to fetch. Values: CORRESPONDENCE, WORKLOG, ANNOUNCEMENTS, SYNOPSIS, AI_AUTOMATIONS. Use [] for metadata only.
- maxCorrespondence/maxWorklogs: number (1-100, default 100). Use 1 for latest only.
- includeEngagements/includeMedic: boolean (default true)
- includeHolds: boolean (default false)

Comments in the response include `commentId` which can be used with the `update-comment` write action.

When `includeHolds` is true, the response includes `holdDetails`: an array of hold objects with `state` (OK | ALARM | INSUFFICIENT_DATA), `lastTransitionDate`, `arn`, `name`, `type`, `region`, and `url`. Returns `null` if the holds endpoint is unavailable. If some holds failed to resolve, `holdErrors` (an array of error objects) is also present, signaling that `holdDetails` is incomplete.

Example (metadata only): { "action": "get-ticket", "input": { "ticketId": "ABC123", "threads": [] } }

### get-my-resolver-groups
Get resolver groups the current user belongs to. No parameters.

### get-resolver-group-details
Get resolver group configuration, members, and settings. Parameters: groupName

### get-resolver-group-labels
Get labels for tickets in a resolver group. Returns each label's `id` (GUID) and `name`; `"inherited": true` marks labels from a parent folder. Use `id` values with `labels:<GUID>` in search-tickets queries to filter by label.
Parameters: groupName (required).

### get-search-instructions
Get comprehensive search field descriptions, query syntax, and best practices. No parameters.

### get-resolver-groups-for-cti
Get resolver groups for a CTI. Use to find the correct assignedGroup before creating a ticket.
Parameters: category, type, item (all required).

### get-rollup-resolver-groups-for-login
Get all resolver groups that roll up to a given login's ownership chain.
Parameters: login (required).

tools.description:
Retrieves the current status and health metrics for a list of pipelines.

    The response includes:
    - Whether the pipeline is enabled
    - The fitness badge (gold, silver, bronze)
    - Health metrics like failed builds, deployments, and tests
    - Pending approvals and workflow steps
    - Basic pipeline information
    - Optional pipeline release metrics when metricsEnabled is true

    Pipeline metrics include:
    - Stage approval and deployment timings
    - Operator intervention counts (manual merges, builds, deployments, etc.)
    - Inventory age and freshness information
    - Version set freshness scores
    - Blockage time and fitness indicators
    - Age of production deployed code
    - Release time estimates
    - Management chain information

    Known metric IDs include: InterventionsPerDeployment, AgeOfProdDeployedMerge, BlockageTime,
    StageApprovalTime, StageDeploymentTime, VersionSetFreshness, OptimisticFullReleaseTime,
    PipelinesFitnessBlockage, OperatorInterventions:* (example OperatorInterventions:ManualApproval).
    Release stage qualifiers use colon syntax (InterventionsPerDeployment:PreProd) and are limited to either PreProd or Prod.
    Omit "metricsFieldNames" to fetch all available metrics.

    Health metrics definitions:
    - failedBuilds: total failing source code builds
    - failedDeployments: total failing deployments
    - failedProdDeployments: total failing deployments to Production fleets
    - failedTests: total failing automated tests
    - failedProdTests: total failing automated tests on Production fleets
    - pendingManualApprovals: total manual approvals waiting for input
    - pendingProdManualApprovals: total manual approvals gating Production deployments waiting for input
    - pendingManualWFSteps: total workflow steps requiring manual approval waiting for input
    - pendingProdManualWFSteps: total workflow steps requiring manual approval and gating Production deployments waiting for input
    - disabledPromotions: number of disabled promotions
    - pipelineDisabled: whether pipeline is admin disabled 0 = false, 1 = true

    If any of these health metrics is non-zero or if the pipeline is disabled then the pipeline is Blocked, meaning it requires operator intervention to continue promoting changes automatically.

    Use the optional 'onlyBlocked' parameter to filter results to only include pipelines that are blocked (either disabled or have health metric issues). Prefer this option over manually identifying blocked pipelines, as it is more efficient.

    Set diagnoseFailedDeployments=true to get CloudFormation stack failure details for failed deployments. Recommended when pipelines show failed deployments to enable faster troubleshooting.

tools.name: QuipEditor
tools.description:
Retrieves and edits Quip documents.

Common usage patterns:
1. Create new document from file: contentFilePath="doc.md", format="markdown" (Quip infers title from first heading)
2. Create new document with explicit title: title="My Document", content="content here", format="markdown"
2. Read document with structure: documentId="ABC123", analyzeStructure=true
3. Add content after heading: documentId="ABC123", location=6, documentRange="Subsection 1.1", content="new", format="markdown"
4. Append to document: documentId="ABC123", content="new", format="markdown" default location 0=APPEND
5. Get section IDs for targeting: documentId="ABC123", returnSectionIds=true
6. Add list item: documentId="ABC123", location=10, sectionId="temp:C:ABC123", content="* New item", format="markdown"

Location parameter guide:
0=APPEND end of document DEFAULT
1=PREPEND beginning of document
2=AFTER_SECTION after section specified by sectionId
3=BEFORE_SECTION before section specified by sectionId
4=REPLACE_SECTION ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE replace section content
5=DELETE_SECTION ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE deletes section
6=AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE after heading specified by documentRange
7=BEFORE_DOCUMENT_RANGE before heading specified by documentRange
8=REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE replace heading AND all content below it
9=DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE deletes heading AND all content below it
10=AFTER_LIST_ITEM smart list insert after specified list item sectionId
11=BEFORE_LIST_ITEM smart list insert before specified list item sectionId

Tips:
- Table cells: use location=4 with composite sectionId (temp:s:temp:C:ROW_ID_temp:C:CELL_ID), plain text content
- Add table rows: use location=2/3 with table-row sectionId, format="html", markdown UNSUPPORTED
- Use analyzeStructure=true first to see available headings for documentRange
- Use returnSectionIds=true to get section IDs for precise targeting
- For adding content after headings like "Subsection 1.1", use location=6 with documentRange="Subsection 1.1"
- Prefer format="markdown" for most content

Markdown List Rules:
- Unordered lists MUST use * instead of - for list markers
- 4 spaces OR tab MUST be used to nest list items
- An additional newline MUST be between list label and its start
- REQUIRED extra newline between label and first list item
Example:
```
**Label:**

* Item one
    * Item one A
* Item two
```
Note: Prefer location=10 (AFTER_LIST_ITEM) or location=11 (BEFORE_LIST_ITEM) with sectionId from a list item for updates. These operations handle parent heading replacement for reliable nested list updates.

⚠️ CRITICAL WARNINGS:
- REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=8 replaces the heading AND ALL CONTENT below until next heading of same level, ensure 'content' FULLY accounts for this
- Renaming ONLY a heading requires manually recreating the section structure
- Document ranges include subheadings: "Section 1" includes "Subsection 1.1", "Subsection 1.2", etc.
- Consider using AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=6 + DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=9 for complex restructuring

<Rule>REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=8) destroys all content to EOF when no same-level heading follows the target — only use when a same-level heading exists below, otherwise use AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=6) + DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=9)</Rule>
<Rule>ALWAYS use analyzeStructure=true first on a document to understand exact structure and observe what content will be affected</Rule>

documentId.description: Quip document URL or ID. Examples: 'quip-amazon.com/ABC123/Doc' or 'ABC123'. OMIT for creation

content.description: HTML or Markdown content to add/edit. Max 1MB. REQUIRED

format.description: Format of content. REQUIRED - must be explicitly specified, prefer 'markdown'

contentFilePath.description: Local filepath to read content from. Takes precedence over 'content' field

sectionId.description: Section ID for targeted operations. Find in HTML IDs. REQUIRED for locations 2-5 (section operations) and 10-11 (list item operations)

documentRange.description: Heading text for document range operations. Must match exact heading text. Example: 'Subsection 1.1' or 'Topic 2 - Prerequisites'. REQUIRED for locations 6-9 - document range operations. Use analyzeStructure=true first to see headings

Retrieves a detailed summary of a pipeline's current state, including:

    - Optionally: detailed failure information for builds, tests, and deployments (via includeFailedBuilds, includeFailedTests, includeFailedDeployments, or includeAllFailures flags)

    Definitions:
    - Badge indicates the automation level of the pipeline (gold: fully automated; silver: mostly automated; bronze: partially automated; no badge: not automated)
    - Promotions needing synchronization indicate a newer artifact is ready to be deployed to the next target in the pipeline
    - failuresSummary provides detailed metadata about each failure including timestamps, IDs, URLs, and actionable troubleshooting information

Retrieves the current status and health metrics for a list of pipelines.

    The response includes:
    - Whether the pipeline is enabled
    - The fitness badge (gold, silver, bronze)
    - Health metrics like failed builds, deployments, and tests
    - Pending approvals and workflow steps
    - Basic pipeline information
    - Optional pipeline release metrics when metricsEnabled is true

    Pipeline metrics include:
    - Stage approval and deployment timings
    - Operator intervention counts (manual merges, builds, deployments, etc.)
    - Inventory age and freshness information
    - Version set freshness scores
    - Blockage time and fitness indicators
    - Age of production deployed code
    - Release time estimates
    - Management chain information

    Known metric IDs include: InterventionsPerDeployment, AgeOfProdDeployedMerge, BlockageTime,
    StageApprovalTime, StageDeploymentTime, VersionSetFreshness, OptimisticFullReleaseTime,
    PipelinesFitnessBlockage, OperatorInterventions:* (example OperatorInterventions:ManualApproval).
    Release stage qualifiers use colon syntax (InterventionsPerDeployment:PreProd) and are limited to either PreProd or Prod.
    Omit "metricsFieldNames" to fetch all available metrics.

    Health metrics definitions:
    - failedBuilds: total failing source code builds
    - failedDeployments: total failing deployments
    - failedProdDeployments: total failing deployments to Production fleets
    - failedTests: total failing automated tests
    - failedProdTests: total failing automated tests on Production fleets
    - pendingManualApprovals: total manual approvals waiting for input
    - pendingProdManualApprovals: total manual approvals gating Production deployments waiting for input
    - pendingManualWFSteps: total workflow steps requiring manual approval waiting for input
    - pendingProdManualWFSteps: total workflow steps requiring manual approval and gating Production deployments waiting for input
    - disabledPromotions: number of disabled promotions
    - pipelineDisabled: whether pipeline is admin disabled 0 = false, 1 = true

    If any of these health metrics is non-zero or if the pipeline is disabled then the pipeline is Blocked, meaning it requires operator intervention to continue promoting changes automatically.

    Use the optional 'onlyBlocked' parameter to filter results to only include pipelines that are blocked (either disabled or have health metric issues). Prefer this option over manually identifying blocked pipelines, as it is more efficient.

    Set diagnoseFailedDeployments=true to get CloudFormation stack failure details for failed deployments. Recommended when pipelines show failed deployments to enable faster troubleshooting.

Search source code in Amazon's code repositories. Results depend on search type:

1. Semantic search (preferred): Returns full source code of matching code elements with pagination
2. Code search: Returns code snippets matching exact strings, symbols, or Boolean queries with pagination
3. Repository search: Returns matching repositories with pagination

Decision guide:
- Always start with 'semantic' for the initial search — user prompts typically contain natural language without specific keywords
- Semantic search returns full source code of matched elements and has a much higher hit rate than code search
- Only use 'code' when you need: an exact literal string match or Boolean query logic (AND/OR/NOT)
- Want to discover packages by name? → Use 'repositories'
- 'semantic' returned no results? → Retry with 'code' using keyword terms and filters
- 'code' returned empty results? → Retry with 'semantic' using natural language description of what you're looking for

<Rule>Code search results only show snippets; semantic search results contain the full source content of each code element. Use ReadInternalWebsites with URL like code.amazon.com/packages/{REPOSITORY}/blobs/{BRANCH}/--/{FILE_PATH} to see surrounding file context if needed</Rule>
<Rule>This tool searches across ALL Amazon repositories. Use local workspace tools (grep, find, WorkspaceSearch) for searching within the current workspace only</Rule>

- IT: Information Technology (IT) Services (IT support documentation, guides, and resources)

- LIST_ARCHIVE: Email List Archive (archived email communications)
- PHONETOOL: Phone Tool (employee directory and organizational information).
- POLICY: Amazon Policy (corporate policies and guidelines)

Get domain details: { "query": "about-domain:SAGE_HORDE" }

Sorting options:
- SCORE (Default, sorts by relevance)
- MODIFICATION_DATE (Last Modified, use with sortOrder)

Examples:
1. { "query": "all hands" }
2. { "query": "Brazil workspace setup", "domain": "BUILDER_HUB" }
3. { "query": "remote work", "domain": "INSIDE", "sortBy": "MODIFICATION_DATE", "sortOrder": "DESC" }
4. { "query": "API guide", "prefixFilters": ["https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/MyTeam"] }

Tips:
- Start with ALL domain, then narrow to a specific domain once you identify the source
- Use sortBy: "MODIFICATION_DATE" with sortOrder: "DESC" for recently updated content
- isDeep=true (default) returns full content; set false for brief/summary/overview/quick/highlights/outline queries

Filter syntax (append to query string):
- Use prefixFilters (max 5) to scope to specific URL paths; omit domain when filtering across multiple domains
- To filter by Wiki page owner: 'owner_group:<name>' or 'owner_group:"name with spaces"' for groups, 'owner_login:<alias>' for direct owner, 'supervisor_chain:<alias>' for org hierarchy (all reports under that person; use when user says 'under <person>' or '<person>'s org'; large result counts are expected). For owner_group only: prefix posix$/ldap$ only if user specifies.
- `owner_group:` accepts a posix/ldap group id or an official Team Name/Id (case-insensitive). If you confidently know both forms for a team, emit both as separate filters (example `owner_group:kis-team owner_group:"Knowledge Ingestion and Search"`); if you only know one, pass it verbatim — don't guess the other.
- To filter by Broadcast channel ID: append 'channel:<id>' per channel (example: 'videos channel:2622 channel:3001')
- Multiple filters of the same type combine in one query — do NOT split into separate tool calls (example 'onboarding guide owner_login:xuezhen owner_login:neelvisw' or 'runbook owner_group:internal-search-team owner_group:kis-team')

[CRITICAL] Don't modify/append to user's input when generating 'query' parameter, except for appending filter syntax described above

[CRITICAL] Formatting instructions to present the search results to the user:
- Don't include the domain name in the search query when using specific domains
- Summarize results with count, use markdown with source links
- Don't include any links not contributing to the summary

# Explains how to use a specific Mechanic tool

## Purpose
- Provides detailed usage information for a specific Mechanic tool
- The tool must exist in order to be explained
- Use this before executing a tool to understand its parameters and options

## Parameter Handling Rules
- If a tool's parameter is required, you need to pass it with a value to the MechanicRunTool 
- Don't attempt to guess parameter values, ask the user what you should use
- For sensitive or specific parameters, always prompt the user for the correct values

## Resource Identification Rules
- If a tool requires a Log Group or an EC2 instance ID and the user didn't explicitly provide it:
  - Use other Mechanic tools that can list these resources
  - For EC2 instances: Use aws ec2 describe-instances
  - For CloudWatch Log Groups: Use aws cloudwatch logs describe-log-groups
- Never guess an EC2 instance ID or CloudWatch Log Group name
- Always look up resource identifiers with the appropriate discovery tool

## Workflow Integration
- After explaining a tool, suggest using MechanicRunTool with the proper parameters
- Include examples of how to use the tool with common parameter combinations

# Mechanic Tool Discovery Guide

## What is Mechanic
- Internal Amazon service providing CLI/web interface for operations
- Safer than AWS CLI with built-in guardrails and risk categorization
- Targets EC2 instances, Apollo hosts/hostclasses, ECS tasks
- Provides networking, logs, system information, and more

## Critical Discovery Rules
- ALWAYS verify tool exists in search results before suggesting
- NEVER assume tools exist based on naming conventions
- Show multiple options if unclear which tool helps user
- Use MechanicDescribeTool after discovery to get usage details
- If describe fails, tool doesn't exist - search again with different keywords

## Usage Best Practices
- Prefer batch operations with multiple values over separate commands
- Look for [Item1,Item2]... notation indicating multi-value support
- Chain multiple commands when single tool doesn't solve problem
- Ask about log limits when fetching logs if tool supports it
- If multiple tools are needed, discover them in the same command with multiple keywords

## Workflow Reference

# Mechanic Tools Workflow Guide

## Required 3-Step Process
1. DISCOVER → MechanicDiscoverTools (find tools)
2. DESCRIBE → MechanicDescribeTool (understand usage)
3. EXECUTE → MechanicRunTool (run with parameters)

## Critical Rule: Use MCP Tools Only
- ALWAYS use MechanicRunTool MCP tool
- NEVER execute mechanic CLI directly
- MCP provides validation, error handling, telemetry, and standardized output

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### 1. Discovery (MechanicDiscoverTools)
- Use relevant keywords to find appropriate tools
- Present multiple options if unsure
- If results don't match user needs: Explain and adjust keywords
- AWS resources: Search "aws" namespace first

### 2. Description (MechanicDescribeTool)
- Never skip this step - provides critical usage details
- Learn required/optional parameters and formats
- Always confirm with user that this is the correct tool

### 3. Execution (MechanicRunTool)
- Format parameters as string array
- Ask user for unknown required values
- Summarize what tool will do before executing
- Show errors to user for troubleshooting

## Common Patterns

### AWS Resource Operations
1. Discover listing tools ("ec2 list", "cloudwatch logs")
2. Execute listing tool to get resource IDs
3. Discover operation tools for those resources
4. Execute operation with obtained IDs

### Troubleshooting Sequence
1. General system information tools
2. Component-specific diagnostics
3. Detailed log analysis tools

## Best Practices
- Follow complete workflow for every operation
- Explain reasoning when searching for tools
- Break complex operations into multiple tool executions
- Return to discovery if tool doesn't solve problem
- Keep user informed at each step

Retrieves and edits Quip documents.

Common usage patterns:
1. Create new document from file: contentFilePath="doc.md", format="markdown" (Quip infers title from first heading)
2. Create new document with explicit title: title="My Document", content="content here", format="markdown"
2. Read document with structure: documentId="ABC123", analyzeStructure=true
3. Add content after heading: documentId="ABC123", location=6, documentRange="Subsection 1.1", content="new", format="markdown"
4. Append to document: documentId="ABC123", content="new", format="markdown" default location 0=APPEND
5. Get section IDs for targeting: documentId="ABC123", returnSectionIds=true
6. Add list item: documentId="ABC123", location=10, sectionId="temp:C:ABC123", content="* New item", format="markdown"

Location parameter guide:
0=APPEND end of document DEFAULT
1=PREPEND beginning of document
2=AFTER_SECTION after section specified by sectionId
3=BEFORE_SECTION before section specified by sectionId
4=REPLACE_SECTION ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE replace section content
5=DELETE_SECTION ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE deletes section
6=AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE after heading specified by documentRange
7=BEFORE_DOCUMENT_RANGE before heading specified by documentRange
8=REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE replace heading AND all content below it
9=DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE deletes heading AND all content below it
10=AFTER_LIST_ITEM smart list insert after specified list item sectionId
11=BEFORE_LIST_ITEM smart list insert before specified list item sectionId

Tips:
- Table cells: use location=4 with composite sectionId (temp:s:temp:C:ROW_ID_temp:C:CELL_ID), plain text content
- Add table rows: use location=2/3 with table-row sectionId, format="html", markdown UNSUPPORTED
- Use analyzeStructure=true first to see available headings for documentRange
- Use returnSectionIds=true to get section IDs for precise targeting
- For adding content after headings like "Subsection 1.1", use location=6 with documentRange="Subsection 1.1"
- Prefer format="markdown" for most content

Markdown List Rules:
- Unordered lists MUST use * instead of - for list markers
- 4 spaces OR tab MUST be used to nest list items
- An additional newline MUST be between list label and its start
- REQUIRED extra newline between label and first list item
Example:
```
**Label:**

* Item one
    * Item one A
* Item two
```
Note: Prefer location=10 (AFTER_LIST_ITEM) or location=11 (BEFORE_LIST_ITEM) with sectionId from a list item for updates. These operations handle parent heading replacement for reliable nested list updates.

⚠️ CRITICAL WARNINGS:
- REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=8 replaces the heading AND ALL CONTENT below until next heading of same level, ensure 'content' FULLY accounts for this
- Renaming ONLY a heading requires manually recreating the section structure
- Document ranges include subheadings: "Section 1" includes "Subsection 1.1", "Subsection 1.2", etc.
- Consider using AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=6 + DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE location=9 for complex restructuring

<Rule>REPLACE_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=8) destroys all content to EOF when no same-level heading follows the target — only use when a same-level heading exists below, otherwise use AFTER_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=6) + DELETE_DOCUMENT_RANGE (location=9)</Rule>

- Run ID only: 123456

Four modes of operation:
- Line: Display specific lines from a test run log file or text artifact file
  - Supports 1-based line numbers (1 = first line)
  - Negative numbers count from end (-1 = last line, -10 = 10th from end)
  - Default: returns up to 50 lines (configurable via maxTotalLines)

  - Supports text or regex (case-insensitive)
  - Shows matches with surrounding context
  - For artifacts, requires path parameter

- Directory: List test artifacts with path navigation and depth control
  - Output format: simplified ls-style without permissions
